note: The reference environment NFR-01's acceptance measurement must run on. A number from anywhere else is a regression metric, not an acceptance result, and bench/append.mjs says which it produced. Every constraint here is evaluated by qualifyRun() in bench/precision.mjs, which REFUSES to run if a constraint declared here has no evaluator — a threshold the code ignores is worse than no threshold, and node_major_at_least was exactly that until a review found it.
excluded: a shared CI runner, where neighbours move the tail by a factor of two
a machine under other load, which is what max_load_average_1m is for
a filesystem at or near capacity, which measurably slows file creation
attestation_note: CPU count, memory and load average cannot establish that a machine is dedicated or that its storage is comparable: a large enough shared runner would satisfy all three. So an acceptance run additionally requires the operator to name the machine and describe its storage (--machine, --storage), and those strings are recorded in the result. This does not make the claim verifiable by a third party; it makes it attributable, which is the honest limit of what a benchmark can assert about its own host.
